sections.content: How many people are "actuaries, economists and statisticians"?

36,245 people

were counted on the census as "actuaries, economists and statisticians" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Actuaries, economists and statisticians assess risk and formulate probabilistic outcomes to inform economic and business policy, they may analyse and interpret data used to assist in the formulation of financial, business and economic policies in order to maximise growth or improve business performance.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "actuaries, economists and statisticians", 24.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "actuaries, economists and statisticians" was 16 to 19 years.

  • data analysts

  • beauticians and related occupations

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "actuaries, economists and statisticians" there were more men than women (66.7% compared with 33.3%).

This means "actuaries, economists and statisticians" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 66.7% and women made up 33.3% of "actuaries, economists and statisticians"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "actuaries, economists and statisticians" included:

  • managers and directors in the creative industries
  • market and street traders and assistants
  • planning, process and production technicians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "actuaries, economists and statisticians" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "actuaries, economists and statisticians" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "actuaries, economists and statisticians", 6.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (92.3% compared with 7.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (94.5%) than self-employed (5.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Tower Hamlets, this is in the same region of London.
